_readme: Industry editions: the same model and the same questions, in each audience's language. Answers are stored on the same steps, so the analysis and report work for every edition.

nonprofit.name: Nonprofit edition
nonprofit.intro: The Diagnostic in the language of nonprofits: board, staff, volunteers, donors and the community, across all of The IV Phases™.

prompts.n1: Our mission provides clear direction for the nonprofit and its programs.
prompts.n2: Our board and staff leadership share a clear understanding of our vision.
prompts.n5: Our program and funding priorities reflect our mission and vision.
prompts.n6: Staff and volunteers understand how their work contributes to our mission.
prompts.n8: Our nonprofit has a clear understanding of what makes our approach to the community distinctive.
prompts.n10: Our foundation gives us a strong platform for growing our impact.
prompts.n11: What is one leadership or organizational strength you believe your nonprofit does particularly well?
prompts.n12: We have a clear process for turning program priorities into action.
prompts.n13: Board members and staff leaders understand how important decisions are made.
prompts.n14: Ownership of key decisions between the board and staff is clear.
prompts.n15: Board, leadership and management responsibilities are understood.
prompts.n16: We regularly evaluate progress toward our program and impact goals.
prompts.n18: Leaders have the information they need, including program data, to make informed decisions.
prompts.n19: Our planning considers our mission goals, our funding and the capacity of staff and volunteers.
prompts.n20: We communicate effectively with staff, volunteers, donors and partners when priorities change.
prompts.n21: Our management practices support our ability to grow our impact.
prompts.n22: What planning, management, or leadership practice currently helps your nonprofit operate effectively?
prompts.n24: Communication expectations are clear for staff, volunteers and the board.
prompts.n26: Performance expectations are understood by staff and volunteers.
prompts.n27: Program teams understand what successful delivery looks like.
prompts.n28: Feedback from staff, volunteers and the people we serve contributes to improvement.
prompts.n29: Our internal systems support collaboration between staff, volunteers and partners.
prompts.n30: Staff and volunteers understand how organizational decisions affect their work.
prompts.n31: Our leadership practices remain consistent through funding pressure or change.
prompts.n32: Our internal systems support continued program quality as we grow.
prompts.n33: What aspect of your culture, communication, or day-to-day operations is currently one of your nonprofit's greatest strengths?
prompts.n34: Important knowledge about programs, donors and partners is accessible beyond individual leaders.
prompts.n35: We intentionally develop future staff and board leaders.
prompts.n36: Executive and board responsibilities can be transferred effectively.
prompts.n38: Our culture can be carried forward as staff, volunteers and board members change.
prompts.n39: Our impact does not depend entirely on one individual, such as a founder or executive director.
prompts.n41: We have considered the legacy we want the nonprofit to leave in the community.
prompts.n43: We are building something that will serve the community beyond the current generation of leaders.
prompts.n44: What is one thing about your nonprofit's knowledge, culture, leadership, or legacy that you most want to preserve?
prompts.n45: What do you want your nonprofit to be able to do, preserve, or become for the community because you built it?

small-enterprise.name: Small Enterprise edition
small-enterprise.intro: The Diagnostic in the language of owner-led businesses: the owner, employees, customers and cash flow, across all of The IV Phases™.

prompts.n1: Our mission provides clear direction for the business.
prompts.n2: The owner and leadership team share a clear understanding of our vision.
prompts.n5: Our business priorities reflect our mission and vision.
prompts.n6: Employees understand how their work contributes to the business and its customers.
prompts.n8: Our business has a clear understanding of what makes us distinctive to our customers.
prompts.n10: Our foundation gives us a strong platform for sustainable growth.
prompts.n11: What is one leadership or organizational strength you believe your business does particularly well?
prompts.n12: We have a clear process for turning business priorities into action.
prompts.n13: The owner and managers understand how important decisions are made.
prompts.n14: Ownership of key decisions is clear, including what the owner no longer has to decide alone.
prompts.n15: Owner, management and team responsibilities are understood.
prompts.n16: We regularly evaluate progress toward our business goals.
prompts.n18: Leaders have the information they need, including financial and customer data, to make informed decisions.
prompts.n19: Our planning considers business goals, cash flow and the capacity of our team.
prompts.n20: We communicate effectively with employees and customers when priorities or circumstances change.
prompts.n21: Our management practices support the business's ability to grow.
prompts.n22: What planning, management, or leadership practice currently helps your business operate effectively?
prompts.n26: Performance expectations are understood by every employee.
prompts.n27: Teams understand what successful delivery to customers looks like.
prompts.n28: Feedback from employees and customers contributes to improvement.
prompts.n29: Our internal systems and tools support collaboration.
prompts.n30: Employees understand how business decisions affect their work.
prompts.n31: Our leadership practices remain consistent during busy seasons, pressure or change.
prompts.n32: Our internal systems support continued performance as the business grows.
prompts.n33: What aspect of your culture, communication, or day-to-day operations is currently one of your business's greatest strengths?
prompts.n34: Important knowledge about customers, suppliers and operations is accessible beyond the owner.
prompts.n35: We intentionally develop the people who could lead the business next.
prompts.n36: The owner's responsibilities could be transferred effectively.
prompts.n38: Our culture can be carried forward as the business evolves.
prompts.n39: Our success does not depend entirely on the owner or any one individual.
prompts.n41: We have considered the legacy we want the business to create, including how it could be sold or handed on.
prompts.n43: We are building a business that can create value beyond the current owner.
prompts.n44: What is one thing about your business's knowledge, culture, leadership, or legacy that you most want to preserve?
prompts.n45: What do you want your business to be able to do, preserve, or become because you built it?
